report_paragraph: Our first two submissions scored 0.44705 public / 0.43278 private (LightGBM LambdaRank ranker) and 0.44688 / 0.43848 (hybrid ranker with course-method features). The hybrid is better on the full test (mean 0.44268 vs 0.43992), but the 630-user public half ranked them the other way, so public differences below about 0.003 say little about model quality. The remaining uploads were fixed in advance from offline evidence rather than from leaderboard feedback: they rank-average rankers trained on two readings of the target (screen time summed over sessions, or the longest single session, which give identical top-5 sets for only 70.5-80.8% of users across folds) and vary the eight-week test history between weeks 15-19 + 28-30 and weeks 20-24 + 28-30. Offline checks could not settle the history choice: the closest proxy comparison was inconclusive, and in weeks 20-24 214 of the 1,260 submission users have no airing watched to 80% or more, against 43 in weeks 15-19. Because the course grades the public score, the graded file is the upload with the highest public score, re-uploaded unchanged as the last submission if a later upload scored lower, while model quality is reported by cross-validation and by the mean of public and private scores rather than by the best public score, which is a maximum over several noisy draws and overstates quality.

reviewer_disagreements_resolved: S3 file: eD (EV-maximizer, skeptic) vs eAD (risk-manager). Resolved: eD first, as det_ens_D. It gives the cleanest read on the one open question (history D vs A), which drives S4. With the S5 lock-in its large spread (SE about 0.0043 vs sub02) is upside only. Putting the hedge second also makes the likely last upload the lower-variance file. My numpy simulation (scratchpad mc.py; noise per differing item calibrated on se_630 = 0.00189) puts eD-first at or above eAD-first by 0.00004-0.00013 in every scenario. That is a practical tie, so information and the safety of the last file decide.

S4 rule: always eAD (EV-maximizer) vs adaptive (risk-manager: eD/eA at 0.44688 after eAD; skeptic: eAD/eA at 0.44588 after eD). Resolved: adaptive on public(S3): det_ens_AD if >= 0.44588, else det_ens_A. The gain is tiny (<= 0.0002 in every simulation). But when D is visibly bad on the public half, eA is both the better second draw and the safer last file.

S5 default: explore (EV-maximizer) vs lock-in (risk-manager, skeptic). Resolved: lock-in by default, exploration only after written confirmation that the best public counts. Both simulations give a break-even P(last) of about 0.24-0.31. The lock-in costs only about 0.0004-0.0005 if best counts, while an exploring S5 under last-submission grading ended below 0.44705 in 30-44% of simulated cases. The task asks for robustness to the unknown rule, and the lock-in gives best = last = selected >= 0.44705 under all of them.

sub03: the EV-maximizer keeps it as an S5 branch; the other two say never. Resolved: never as S3 or S4, because it is dominated by the D label ensemble (1038 identical sets, no label hedge). It is allowed, as det_sum_recent8, only as the S5 exploration under confirmed best-public grading when det_ens_D leads.

Kaggle selection: best + eAD (EV-maximizer) vs best only, with a second only if >= 0.44705 (risk-manager) vs best + next best (skeptic). Resolved: tick only the best-public file; if two are required, add the next-highest public. The grade is a public number, so an offline-preferred second selection can only add ambiguity. Never select by private.

Prior on history D: 'small positive' (EV-maximizer), 'overstated' (risk-manager), 'a bet' (skeptic). Resolved: neutral to slightly negative for submission users. The closest proxy analog gives +0.00102 all / -0.00833 sub. I verified that 214 vs 43 submission users have an empty older block. The proxy re-run drifts by up to 0.00225. The predict_test.py comment 'supported by evidence/history_proxy.json' overstates the evidence and should be corrected. The plan is robust to the prior: the simulation ranking holds from h0 = -0.0015 to +0.0015 and in a pessimistic case with no label or ensemble gain.

Under the official sum reading it fails playbook section 2.5 (F0 all -0.00031, F2 sub -0.00098), and part of its F1 gain may be seed averaging (single-seed spread 0.0028 sub in experiments3_F1.json).
